prompt_architecture.notes: Prompts are assembled from reusable fragments to reduce duplication and keep contract language stable.

base.description: Optimized extraction rules: consolidated JSON-only constraints (5->3) + CONCISE OUTPUT block (descriptions/evidence/empty-field trimming). Verified 2026-08-03: response tokens -14%, LLM duration -25%.
base.template:
Extract entities, relationships, and attributes.

CRITICAL OUTPUT CONSTRAINTS:
- Output ONLY valid JSON: start with `{` and end with `}`. No reasoning, commentary, markdown fences, or prefix text.
- Do NOT wrap output in code fences (no ```json). If you need to think, do it silently.
- Response must contain JSON and nothing else.

CONCISE OUTPUT (save tokens):
- descriptions: max 2 sentences.
- evidence content: max 50 chars, quote key phrase only.
- Omit empty attributes and empty optional fields.
- Use short meta_id values (e.g. L1-001, L2-002).

TEMPORAL FIELD EXTRACTION (when available from source):
- valid_from: extract effectivity date / start date when the document specifies one (ISO 8601 preferred, e.g. 2026-01-15).
- version / revision: extract version or revision info when the document specifies one (e.g. v1.2, Rev A, 3.0).
- timestamp: when the document mentions dates, include a timestamp field inside evidence (ISO 8601 preferred).

technical.description: Strict layer constraints with L1 fixed enumeration and Asset priority
technical.template:
Extract entities AND relationships{domain_hint}.

## CLASSIFICATION RULES
- CLASSES: Capability, System, Actor, Asset, Data, Process, Concept, BusinessScenario, BusinessRule, MappingRule, ValidationRule
- NAMING: TitleCase, noun, singular
- EVIDENCE: REQUIRED (exact quote from document)
- meta_id: L0/L1/L2/L2.5/L3-prefix

## STRICT LAYER CONSTRAINTS (HARD RULES)

### L0: Core categories (Abstract - ONLY 6-11 categories)
- Definition: Fundamental abstract categories that form the foundation of the ontology
- Examples: ONLY: Capability, System, Actor, Asset, Data, Process, Concept, BusinessScenario, BusinessRule, MappingRule, ValidationRule
- CRITICAL: DO NOT put specific systems (VCATS, CHIMAS, OTA2System) at L0 - they belong at L2

### L1: Fixed enumeration dictionary (NO specific business names!)
- Definition: Abstract subtypes - FIXED ENUMERATION ONLY. L1 is a stable meta-model dictionary.
- ALLOWED L1 VALUES (use these exact names):
  - Actor subtypes: Internal_Department, Business_Function, External_Partner
  - Data subtypes: Master_Data, Transaction_Data, Document
  - System subtypes: SupplyChain_System, Manufacturing_System, Retail_System, Engineering_System
  - Process subtypes: SupplyChain_Process, Manufacturing_Process, Engineering_Process
  - Capability subtypes: CostManagement, ChangeManagement, QualityManagement, RequirementsManagement, RiskManagement, DealerManagement, DocumentManagement, ProcurementManagement
  - Asset subtypes: Vehicle_Asset, Part_Asset, Tooling_Asset
- CRITICAL: DO NOT put specific teams (Cost Management Team), specific data (PartData), or specific systems (TACDIS) in L1!
- CRITICAL: Teams/Departments belong in L2 as Actor, NOT in L1!
- CRITICAL: Specific data entities (PartData, OrderData) belong in L2 as Data, NOT in L1!

### L2: Logical entities (MAIN LAYER - 50-70% of entities!)
- Definition: Macro systems, departments, business processes, and organizational units
- Examples: TACDIS, DMS, PowerBI, Finance Department, Cost Management Team, CRP Process
- Belongs here: Specific systems, named departments, named teams, business workflows
- DO NOT put here: Physical data tables, micro features, specific part instances

### L2.5: Rules/mappings
- Definition: Business rules, validation rules, mapping rules
- Examples: SWDLValidationRule, TARR75Rule, ROI4Rule

### L3: Physical instances (IMPORTANT!)
- Definition: Physical tables, micro features, specific records, part instances, unique identifiers
- Examples: Order Handling Table (physical table), Use Up Countdown (micro feature), VIN: YV1ZZZ99Z9Z9999999, PartNumber: 31254789
- MUST extract: Physical data tables, micro features/capabilities, specific part names (XC60Wheel, SeatStorageBox), VINs, serial numbers
- If document mentions a physical table or micro feature, IT GOES TO L3!


## MANUFACTURING ENTITY DETECTION (CRITICAL for OEM)
- BOP (Bill of Process): MUST be extracted as L2 (Process) - represents factory workstation/sequence
- POS (Point of Service/Physical Position): MUST be extracted as L2 or L3 - represents physical installation position
- PII (Process Instruction Information): MUST be extracted as L2 (Data) - worker operation guidance
- MBOM (Manufacturing BOM): MUST be extracted as L2 (Data) - manufacturing bill of materials
- EBOM (Engineering BOM): MUST be extracted as L2 (Data) - engineering bill of materials
- C-Note (Change Note): MUST be extracted as L2 (Data) - delta data package for changes
- ECN (Engineering Change Note): MUST be extracted as L2 (Process) - change management process
- Effectivity Date / Point of Cut-off: MUST be extracted as L2.5 (ValidationRule) - time-based rules
- Lead Time / Run-out Period: MUST be extracted as attribute or L2.5 rule - inventory transition timing
- Any mention of factory workstations, assembly lines, or production sequences MUST be extracted

## DYNAMIC TIME DIMENSION RULES
- When document mentions "effectivity date", "cut-off date", "phase-in/phase-out", extract as L2.5 ValidationRule
- When document mentions inventory transition (old part run-out, new part introduction), extract timing attributes
- When document mentions shift/schedule constraints, extract as L2.5 rules

## TEMPORAL FIELD EXTRACTION (P2-8)
- valid_from: When the source document specifies an effectivity date / start date for an entity, extract it as the `valid_from` field (ISO 8601 preferred, e.g. 2026-01-15). Leave empty if not available.
- version / revision: When the source document specifies version or revision info (e.g. v1.2, Rev A, 3.0), extract it as the `version` field. Leave empty if not available.
- timestamp in evidence: When the document mentions dates relevant to an entity, include a `timestamp` field inside the entity's evidence object (ISO 8601 preferred).

## ASSET PRIORITY RULES (CRITICAL)
- Any mention of physical parts (wheel, seat, valve, engine, battery, chassis) MUST be classified as Asset class
- Any mention of vehicles (VIN, car model) MUST be classified as Asset class
- Any mention of tooling/molds/fixtures MUST be classified as Asset class
- DO NOT classify physical parts as Data or Concept - they are Assets!
- Asset entities should be at L2 (logical asset types) or L3 (specific part instances)

## IMPORTANT REQUIREMENTS
1. EXTRACT ALL LAYERS: You MUST extract entities at ALL layers (L0, L1, L2, L2.5, L3)
2. L0 RULE: L0 MUST ONLY contain abstract categories
3. L1 RULE: L1 MUST ONLY contain fixed enumeration values (see allowed list above)
4. HIERARCHY: L2 must reference L1 via parent_id
5. HIERARCHY: L3 must reference L2 via parent_id
6. RELATIONSHIPS: MUST extract relationships between ANY entities
7. L2 PRIORITY: L2 should contain MORE entities than L1
8. L3 INSTANCES: Create L3 for physical tables, micro features, part instances, and unique IDs
9. ASSET EXTRACTION: Actively look for and extract Asset entities (physical parts, vehicles, tooling)

{schema_hint_section}
